question.worked_solution:
We start by writing the root as a rational power, $\sqrt[5]{{x}^{7}}={x}^{7/5}.$ So, we can apply the power rule with $n=\frac{7}{5}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \sqrt[5]{{x}^{7}}\,\text{d}x & =\int {x}^{7/5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{7/5+1}}{(\frac{7}{5}+1)}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{12/5}}{(\frac{12}{5})}+C \\  & =\frac{5{x}^{12/5}}{12}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, let's check by differentiating:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{5{x}^{12/5}}{12}+C) & = \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{5{x}^{12/5}}{12})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) & = \\ \frac{5}{12}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{12/5})+0 & = \\ \frac{5}{12}\cdot \frac{12}{5}{x}^{12/5-1} & = \\ {x}^{7/5}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
